exposure: Diastasis Recti Abdominis (DRA) features (ultrasonographic findings, abdominal midline condition, echo types)
cohort: The study included 143 parturient women diagnosed with DRA and a control group of 57 women without DRA, all aged 21-43 years, who carried a single fetus to term without instrumental delivery or prior abdominal surgery, assessed during the postpartum period.
finding: DRA is prevalent among postpartum women with specific ultrasonographic profiles indicating considerable abdominal muscle separation, and significant differences were found in rectus abdominis separation and levator ani muscle hiatus area, both being larger in the observation group compared to the control group.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was identified as a significant risk factor for DRA occurrence in the logistic regression analysis.
cross-section timing: Postpartum period (specific timing relative to birth not mentioned)
